example: Compare normal extracellular K+ with a large increase outside the cell. With less difference between inside and outside, less K+ leaves, so the membrane becomes less negative.

en.title: How Ion Gradients Create Resting Potential
en.learning_objective: Explain why a K+ concentration gradient plus selective K+ permeability makes a resting neuron's interior negative.
en.simple_explanation: An ion gradient is an unequal concentration of an ion across a membrane. Pumps maintain much more K+ inside the neuron, while the resting membrane is highly permeable to K+ through potassium channels.
en.how_it_works: K+ moves outward through open channels down its concentration gradient. Negative charge is left behind, making the inside negative relative to the outside. The growing electrical attraction pulls K+ inward and opposes further outward diffusion. Their balance produces a stable negative potential near the K+ equilibrium potential.
en.visual:
high K+ inside
      ↓ K+ exits through channels
negative charge remains inside
      ↓
negative resting potential
en.use_case: A clinician observes elevated extracellular K+. Predict the voltage change: the K+ gradient is reduced, so less outward K+ movement is favored and the membrane depolarizes, becoming less negative.
en.expected_result: At rest, the membrane sits near −65 mV. Raising extracellular K+ shifts it toward a less negative value and can impair excitable cells.
en.what_to_notice: A concentration gradient supplies the tendency to move, but selective channels determine which ion strongly influences voltage. Both conditions are necessary.
en.common_mistake: Do not say that all intracellular K+ leaves. Only a small separation of charge is needed before the electrical force opposes further net K+ movement.
en.practical_tip: Trace resting potential in three links: pump-maintained gradient, selective K+ movement, then charge separation.
en.question: Why does outward K+ movement make the neuron's resting interior negative?
en.answer: K+ carries positive charge out, leaving relative negative charge inside until the electrical force balances its outward diffusion.
